messages:
ops-oncall: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — multiple runtime pods in us-east-1-gpu-pool are crashlooping with SIGSEGV. Observed across 3 nodes. Auto-escalated to on-call SRE and runtime eng.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-0191 — Runtime crashloops (segfaults) affecting serving runtime. Pager: @ops-oncall, @maya on-call.
maya: looking now. which deployment? any recent rollouts to gpu-pool?
oliver: seeing surge of OOM/CUDA errors then SIGSEGV in the engine logs. stacktrace points at fused-kernel shared object.
chun: confirmed: pods show repeated restartReason=OOMKilled then OOM -> later SIGSEGV when GPU memory probed. log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T12:01:07Z] runtime: cudaErrorIllegalAddress at 0x7f34... kernel.cu:line 412
[2026-03-15T12:01:07Z] runtime: fatal signal: segmentation fault (SIGSEGV)
Backtrace (most recent call first):
  0x7f34ab12 in fused_attention::dispatch(...) +0x54
  0x7f34a9f3 in runtime_engine::forward(..) +0x1a3
  0x55aa3b in main_loop +0x8f
```
maya: tag in container image? I see recent rollout of image: redwood/runtime:fused-v2.3.9 pushed ~11:45.
oliver: yes that image is the only change in last deploy window. older image fused-v2.3.7 was stable.
ops-oncall: immediate mitigation proposals?
maya: 1) cordon nodes with repeated restarts to prevent new pods scheduling there 2) scale down deployment to 0 or switch image to previous stable 3) enable fallback routing to cpu-pool for customer traffic 4) capture core dumps and upload to S3 for postmortem.
chun: cordoning node-ux-12 and node-ux-14 now (kubectl cordon).
maya: running kubectl -n serving set image deploy/llm-runtime runtime=redwood/runtime:fused-v2.3.7 --record
```
# patch applied
kubectl rollout status deploy/llm-runtime -n serving
```
deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated for deployment llm-runtime to image fused-v2.3.7. Monitoring restarts.
ops-oncall: patch rolled back. Observed immediate decrease in restarts on nodes that got new image.
oliver: still seeing a handful of restarts on one node — looks like leftover pods on older image still failing due to corrupted cached state. I'll drain that node.
chun: draining node-ux-13 to force eviction and reschedule: kubectl drain node-ux-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
support-lucy: notifying customers in the affected region — sending an initial status update: "We are mitigating an issue causing increased errors for some inference requests in US-EAST. No data loss. We'll post updates."
maya: observed metrics: error rate peaked at ~18% for a subset of routes (large context models) between 11:50-12:05. Tail latency spiked. After rollback, error rate fell to ~1.5% within 4 minutes.
oliver: root cause hypothesis: fused kernel in fused-v2.3.9 has a memory aliasing bug exposed under certain sequence length + batch patterns -> illegal memory access. Repro locally with stress harness.
ops-oncall: handoff — @maya needs to sign out in 15. I will hand incident commander to @oliver. Maya, can you capture runbook and current state?
maya: summary: rollback to fused-v2.3.7 complete, cordoned nodes: node-ux-12/14, drained node-ux-13, canary health good. Captured core dumps from two failed pods and uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-20260315-0191/. Links in the incident ticket.
oliver: taking over incident commander. Next steps: block fused-v2.3.9 from further deploys, add canary gating to fused images, run reproducer at scale on qa-gpu, add additional tests for long sequence attention paths. Also schedule urgent revert PR in runtime repo.
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation applied — rollback successful. Impact: partial errors for US-EAST inference (models rtx-large), ~20% customers affected during window.
support-lucy: CS notified top 5 impacted customers, referencing ticket INC-20260315-0191. They requested ETA for fix; resonded with preliminary "fix in progress, full mitigation applied (rollback), engineering triage ongoing".
chun: filing node-flapping follow-up: nodes that had repeated OOMs show ~200MB orphaned memory allocations in nvml before kernel crash. Added a diagnostic job to collect nvml snapshots every 30s for 1 hour.
maya: adding follow-ups to post-incident: 1) enable core_pattern piping to collector, 2) build pre-deploy smoke test that exercises fused kernels with long sequences, 3) add GPU sanitizer build for fused operator.
oliver: created PR to block fused-v2.3.9 in image registry (denylist) and added CI gating. PR: https://git.redwood/internal/pr/4321
ops-oncall: taking incident to severity S2 -> lowering the pager frequency. Will keep monitoring for 1h.
incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-0191 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
maya: quick note for postmortem: root cause likely memory aliasing in fused attention path introduced in commit abc123 (merge from optimization branch). Repro steps, core dumps and logs attached to ticket.
oliver: turning over to postmortem team. If anything new appears ping me directly. I'm updating the runbook and marking follow-up ownerships.
support-lucy: posted status update to status.redwood.io: "Mitigation applied; customers may see reduced errors. Root cause investigation ongoing — we will update with timeline."
ops-oncall: ending handover — on-call signout in 5. thanks all for quick response. reactions: :thumbsup: :party_parrot:
maya: :raised_hands: good teamwork.
incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-0191 -> created follow-up tasks: PM-431 (postmortem), ENG-1198 (revert fused kernel), SRE-77 (core dump collector).
